A foundation service must not loop over its service model type.

What The Standard says

“Pure-Primitive” — Foundation services wrap one primitive dependency operation and must not combine primitive work into higher-order processing. Looping over the service's model would turn one primitive operation into bulk processing. read it here.
“Single Entity” — The Standard keeps a foundation focused on one entity integration and pushes increased orchestration complexity upward. Iterating validation-rule objects remains valid because those rules are not the service model contract. read it here.

Why it matters

A foundation operation should act atomically on its service model rather than becoming a batch workflow. Iterating validation rules is legitimate because it builds one model's validation result; iterating the model contract itself signals processing logic that belongs in the next layer.

Bad code example

// Violates STXF001: A foundation service must not loop over its service model type.
foreach (Student student in students) broker.InsertStudent(student);

Good code example

// Follows STXF001
broker.InsertStudents(students);
